etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French éclectique, from Ancient Greek ἐκλεκτικός (eklektikós, “selective”), from ἐκλέγω (eklégō, “to pick, choose”), from ἐκ (ek, “out, from”) + λέγω (légō, “to choose, count”).
senses: Selecting a mixture of what appears to be best of various doctrines, methods or styles.
Someone who selects according to the eclectic method.
